Moments of the Beta-Binomial in Closed Form

Source: R/moments.R
betabinom_moments.Rd

Returns the mean, the variance, the skewness or the excess kurtosis of the beta-binomial with \(n\) trials, mean proportion \(\mu\) and dispersion \(\sigma = 1/(\alpha + \beta)\), each in a closed form that forms no difference of large raw moments. With \(g = \mu(1-\mu)\), $$E[Y] = n\mu,\qquad \mathrm{Var}(Y) = ng\,\frac{1 + n\sigma}{1 + \sigma},$$ $$\gamma_1 = (1 - 2\mu)\,\frac{1 + 2n\sigma}{1 + 2\sigma} \sqrt{\frac{1 + \sigma}{gn(1 + n\sigma)}},$$ $$\gamma_2 = \frac{6n\sigma(1 + n\sigma)\,[(1 - 6g)(1 + \sigma) + g] + (1 + \sigma)(1 - 6g - \sigma)}{gn(1 + 2\sigma)(1 + 3\sigma)(1 + n\sigma)}.$$ At \(\sigma = 0\) these are the binomial's, \(\gamma_2\) reducing to \((1 - 6g)/(gn)\). The excess kurtosis is written as one quotient, so that it is not formed as a kurtosis near 3 minus 3, which loses the digits of a value of order \(1/n\).

Usage

betabinom_moments(mu, sigma, n, what)

Arguments

mu

The mean proportion, a numeric vector in \((0, 1)\).

sigma

The dispersion, a positive numeric vector.

n

The number of trials, a single positive whole number.

what

One of "mean", "variance", "skewness" or "kurtosis".

Value

A numeric vector of the recycled length of mu and sigma.

See also

mean.BetaBinom1Distrib(), variance.BetaBinom1Distrib(), skewness.BetaBinom1Distrib() and kurtosis.BetaBinom1Distrib(), and the methods of BetaBinom2Distrib, which call it.

Examples

# At a small dispersion the excess kurtosis tends to the binomial's.
distributions7:::betabinom_moments(0.3, 1e-12, 1e6, "kurtosis")
#> [1] -1.238095e-06
(1 - 6 * 0.21) / (0.21 * 1e6)
#> [1] -1.238095e-06
